Leonardo da Vinci.text: Salvator Mundi sold for $450.3 million in 2017. In 1958 it had gone for £45, as a work by one of his pupils.
Leonardo da Vinci.evidence: The painting was sold at auction for US$450.3 million on 15 November 2017 by Christie's in New York ... sold it at auction in 1958 for £45 (equivalent to £900 in 2025) as a work by Leonardo's pupil Giovanni Antonio Boltraffio, to whom the painting remained attributed until 2011.

Willem de Kooning.text: Interchange went to Ken Griffin for $300 million in 2015. De Kooning had sold it in 1955 for $4,000.
Willem de Kooning.evidence: Originally sold by the artist in 1955 for $4,000, it was sold by the David Geffen Foundation to Kenneth C. Griffin for $300 million in September 2015

Paul Cézanne.text: One of his five Card Players went to Qatar's royal family in 2011 for an estimated $250 million, a record until 2017.
Paul Cézanne.evidence: there are five paintings in the series ... One version of The Card Players was sold in 2011 to the Royal Family of Qatar for a price estimated at $250 million ($357.8 million today), signifying a new mark for highest ever price for a painting, not surpassed until November 2017.

Gustav Klimt.text: Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer sold for $236.4 million in 2025. To escape the Nazis, she claimed Klimt was her father.
Gustav Klimt.evidence: On 18 November 2025 ... Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer was sold at Sotheby's in New York for US$236.4 million ... To avoid persecution, Elisabeth obtained a document stating that Klimt was her father

Paul Gauguin.text: When Will You Marry?, painted in Tahiti in 1892, was sold privately to Qatar in 2015 for close to $210 million.
Paul Gauguin.evidence: When Will You Marry? ... is an oil painting from 1892 by the French Post-Impressionist artist Paul Gauguin ... it was sold privately by the family of Rudolf Staechelin to Sheikha Al-Mayassa bint Hamad Al-Thani, in February 2015 for close to US$210 million

Jackson Pollock.text: Ken Griffin paid $200 million for the drip painting Number 17A in 2015. It was in the 1949 Life story that made Pollock famous.
Jackson Pollock.evidence: The piece was featured in the August 1949 edition of Life that made Jackson Pollock a celebrity. It is owned by hedge fund manager Kenneth C. Griffin, who purchased it in September 2015 from David Geffen for $200 million

Rembrandt.text: The Netherlands bought his self-portrait The Standard Bearer from the Rothschilds for €175 million in 2022.
Rembrandt.evidence: The Standard Bearer is a three-quarter-length self-portrait by Rembrandt ... the Rothschild family sold the painting to the Netherlands for €175 million in 2022.

Andy Warhol.text: Shot Sage Blue Marilyn sold for $195 million in 2022. Its series is named for a woman who fired a revolver through four of the canvases.
Andy Warhol.evidence: The paintings acquired their collective title after performance artist Dorothy Podber fired a revolver through a stack of four of the canvases at Warhol's Factory studio in 1964 ... Shot Sage Blue Marilyn, which sold for $195 million in 2022

Mark Rothko.text: Dmitry Rybolovlev paid €140 million for No. 6 (Violet, Green and Red) in 2014; his dealer had bought it for about €80 million.
Mark Rothko.evidence: It was privately bought for €140 million by Dmitry Rybolovlev in 2014 ... Bouvier had actually bought the painting (rather than simply acting as a dealer) from Paiker H.B. for ~€80,000,000 before selling it on to Rybolovlev for €140,000,000.

Pablo Picasso.text: Les Femmes d'Alger (Version O) sold for $179.4 million in 2015. In 1956 a couple bought all 15 in the series for $212,500.
Pablo Picasso.evidence: Les Femmes d'Alger ... is a series of 15 paintings ... The entire series of Les Femmes d'Alger was bought by Victor and Sally Ganz from the Galerie Louise Leiris in Paris for $212,500 in June 1956 ... "Version O" was auctioned at Christie's New York for a second time in May 2015, selling for $179.4 million including fees, a record price for a painting at auction.
